messages:
mike: Quick heads-up — ran a breadthbench pass on the new 11B-open variant (baseline fp16) and an int8 quantized build. Can someone spit out a concise cost-vs-quality snapshot we can hand to GTN/product? looking for unit token delta, throughput, and a short recommendation.

anya: On it. did a fast slice (conv + longform + summarization). Topline: token cost down ~42% vs fp16. Quality changes: longform Rouge-L -0.6, convo-relevance -0.8%, summarization ROUGE1 -0.3.

sanjay: numbers please in a bite-sized format — and what's the baseline tokens/sec on our Dedicated p4d config?

anya: paste: ```
baseline fp16 (p4d): 1200 tok/s
int8 quant (same HW): 1900 tok/s (+58%)
unit cost: fp16 $0.0018/token-equivalent -> int8 $0.00105/token-equivalent (~-42%)
quality (delta vs fp16): convo_relev -0.8%, rougeL_long -0.6, rouge1_sum -0.3
```

lucas: product asks: what's the recommended routing policy? at what quality delta do we trigger fallback to fp16 for critical flows? current guideline in playbook is <=1% utility drop tolerated, right?

mike: yes, default cutoff is 1% absolute utility loss for critical GTN features. For non-critical (low-stakes completion) we can be more aggressive. I suggest:
- Default: int8 for API and non-editor flows.
- Hybrid: route multi-turn sessions >6 turns or prompts >1024 tokens to fp16.
- Canary: start with 10% traffic for int8, monitor recall/CTR/PDQ metrics.

anya: quick econ sim: for 100M tokens/month baseline fp16 -> $180k/mo. If we shift 80% tokens to int8 per rule above, new cost ~ $116k/mo => saving ~$64k/mo. But product slices (editor, longform) will remain on fp16 so savings are lower in reality (~$24k/mo for conservative adoption).

deploy-bot: perf-smoke on staging: int8 build smoke results: shards 3/3, median latency 82ms, p95 210ms, p99 320ms. No OOMs during 30m soak.

anya: quality note: the -0.8% on convo relevance concentrates on rare named-entity followups and long context edits. Short Q/A and single-turn completions show <0.2% delta. So routing by slice buys a lot of the econ.

claire: @mike @anya this looks actionable. product wants a two-line recommendation for GTN: econ + safety/regression guardrails. I'll draft the PD if you confirm wording.

mike: confirm: two-line rec: "Adopt int8 for bulk traffic (non-editor flows) to realize ~30-40% unit cost savings; keep fp16 for multi-turn/longform/editor flows with a 1% utility-drop cutoff and a 10% canary ramp. Monitor convo-relevance and longform Rouge-L; auto-fallback on slices exceeding thresholds." :thumbsup:

anya: adding quick scorecard snippet for PD (for clarity): ```
Scorecard (int8 vs fp16)
- Unit cost delta: -42%
- Median latency: 82ms (int8) vs 130ms (fp16)
- p99: 320ms (int8) vs 480ms (fp16)
- Convo relevance: -0.8% (only in multi-turn NER-heavy slices)
- Longform Rouge-L: -0.6
Operational recs:
- Canary 10% -> 50% -> 80% with weekly quality checkpoints
- Route multi-turn >6 to fp16 by default
- Add a small prompt-level delta monitor (CTR/PDQ) with auto-alert at 0.5% negative drift
```

sanjay: solid. can you drop a short-run flagset for ops? e.g., rollout config we can paste in the routing table?

mike: put this in the routing config: `{"strategy":"slice-based","canary_pct":10,"fallback_on_quality_drop":true,"quality_threshold":1.0,"slices_to_force_fp16":["multi_turn_gt6","longform_>1024"]}`

claire: perfect. I'll attach this thread to the PD and ping GTN. thanks all. :rocket:
